title_en: China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Chengdu Office v. Sichuan Tailai Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd., Sichuan Tailai Housing Development Co., Ltd., and Sichuan Tailai Entertainment Co., Ltd. — dispute over a loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: Where affiliated companies have cross-shareholding relationships, are established by the same legal person, and have the same natural person serving as the legal representative of each company, if such legal representative uses his control over the aforementioned multiple companies to disregard the independent personality of each company, arbitrarily disposes of and confuses the property, creditor's rights, and debt relationships of each company, causing the personnel, property, etc. of each company to be indistinguishable, the corporate personalities of these multiple companies, although ostensibly independent from each other, in substance constitute personality mixing. Therefore, if the legitimate rights and interests of creditors are harmed, these multiple companies shall bear joint and several liability for repayment.

full_text_en:
China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Chengdu Office v. Sichuan Tailai Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd., Sichuan Tailai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Sichuan Tailai Entertainment Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan guaranty contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where affiliated companies have overlapping equity relationships, are established with capital contributions from the same legal person, and have the same natural person acting as the legal representative of each company, if that legal representative, by exercising control over these multiple companies, disregards the independent legal personality of each company, arbitrarily disposes of and confuses the property, creditor's rights, and debt relationships among the companies, resulting in the inability to distinguish the personnel, property, etc., of each company, then although these multiple companies are superficially independent of each other as legal persons, they in substance constitute a confusion of personalities. Consequently, if the legitimate rights and interests of creditors are harmed thereby, these multiple company legal persons shall bear joint and several liability for discharge.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 55

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sichuan Tailai Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Inside Sichuan China Wine City Co., Ltd., Tongzilin Village, Wuhou District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Shen Huayuan, Chairman of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Deng Yong, lawyer at Sichuan Junshida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wen Xiaopeng, lawyer at Beijing Jingyi Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sichuan Tailai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Inside Sichuan China Wine City Co., Ltd., Tongzilin Village, Wuhou District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Shen Huayuan, Chairman of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Deng Yong, lawyer at Sichuan Junshida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wen Xiaopeng, lawyer at Beijing Jingyi Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sichuan Tailai Entertainment Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Inside Sichuan China Wine City Co., Ltd., Tongzilin Village, Wuhou District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Shen Huayuan, Chairman of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: Deng Yong, lawyer at Sichuan Junshida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wen Xiaopeng, lawyer at Beijing Jingyi Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Chengdu Office, domiciled at: Shudu Building, No. 20, Shuwabei Third Street, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.
Responsible Person: Zhong Jin, Director of the Office.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Wei, lawyer at Beijing Zhanda Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Sun Junfu, lawyer at Beijing Zhanda Law Firm.

The appellants, Sichuan Tailai Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Decoration Company), Sichuan Tailai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Real Estate Company), and Sichuan Tailai Entertainment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Entertainment Company), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2007) Chuan Min Chu Zi No. 17 rendered by the Sichuan High People's Court in the case of dispute over loan guaranty contract with the appellee, China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Chengdu Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Chengdu Office). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Pei Yingshuo, and Judges Zhu Hainian and Gong Bangyou to conduct the trial. Court Clerk Zhang Yongshu served as the record-keeper. The case is now concluded.

The Sichuan High People's Court found through trial the following facts:

On October 18, 1999, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company entered into a "Debt Restructuring Agreement" with the Shudu Avenue Sub-branch of Bank of China, Chengdu (hereinafter referred to as BOC Shudu Sub-branch), regarding the restructuring of an overdue loan of RMB 22 million originally held by Decoration Company in the Trust Department of Bank of China, Chengdu Branch. The agreement stipulated that: Decoration Company would assume all principal and overdue interest of the loan; Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company jointly promised to use the various assets and rights formed by the "Southwest Celebrity Club" project developed by Entertainment Company (which was invested in and established by Decoration Company and Real Estate Company) within the China Wine City as collateral for the above loan of Decoration Company; after the guarantee procedures were completed, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company would re-sign the loan contract, mortgage contract, and other relevant supplementary contracts with BOC Shudu Sub-branch. On the same day, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company jointly issued a "Principal and Interest Repayment Plan" to BOC Shudu Sub-branch, promising to use the operating income and other funding sources of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company to fulfill the repayment obligations. On October 19, 1999, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company each issued a "Letter of Guarantee" to BOC Shudu Sub-branch, guaranteeing the use of the various assets and rights of the "Southwest Celebrity Club" project as collateral for the above loan of Decoration Company, and entrusting Decoration Company to sign relevant legal documents and handle related procedures with BOC Shudu Sub-branch.

On November 12, 1999, Decoration Company and BOC Shudu Sub-branch re-signed a "Loan Contract", stipulating: the loan amount was RMB 22 million, with a loan term from November 17, 1999 to November 16, 2002, of which RMB 5 million would be repaid on December 16, 2000, at an annual interest rate of 5.85%; RMB 12 million would be repaid on November 16, 2001, at an annual interest rate of 5.94%; and RMB 5 million would be repaid on November 16, 2002, at an annual interest rate of 5.94%. The interest payment method was quarterly payment, and for the borrower's overdue unpaid interest, liquidated damages would be calculated at a daily rate of 0.21 per thousand. If the borrower failed to repay according to the repayment plan, the lender had the right to charge interest on the overdue portion from the date of default at a daily rate of 0.21 per thousand. The "Loan Contract" also stipulated that all debts under the contract would be guaranteed by the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract". On November 18, 1999, both parties completed the loan disbursement procedures.

On the same day, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and BOC Shudu Sub-branch signed a "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and a "Supplementary Contract to the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplementary Contract"). The "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" stipulated that the scope of mortgage guarantee was all debts under any loan contracts signed between BOC Shudu Sub-branch and Decoration Company during the period from November 17, 1999 to November 16, 2002, with a maximum guarantee limit of RMB 22 million; the mortgaged property consisted of the properties listed in the "Asset Appraisal Report" of Jianhua Certified Public Accountants and the operating rights of the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites and the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant projects as described in the "Supplementary Contract". The "Supplementary Contract" stipulated that the project operating rights referred to in this contract included the trademark usage rights of "Yinmeng Lake" and "Golden Years", the usage rights of the buildings and ancillary buildings where the projects were located, and the ownership of all properties under the projects. The ownership of all properties under the projects referred to the value of the fixed assets of Entertainment Company's "Southwest Celebrity Club" project, namely the renovation and decoration works and equipment of the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites, as listed in the "Asset Appraisal Report" of Jianhua Certified Public Accountants. On November 17, 1999, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and BOC Shudu Sub-branch registered the "Supplementary Contract" with the Sichuan Administration for Industry and Commerce. On December 15, 2000, both parties notarized the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract" (Notarial Deed No. [2000] Cheng Zheng Nei Jing Zi No. 19314). On December 13, 2000, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company again issued a "Principal and Interest Repayment Plan" to BOC Shudu Sub-branch, promising to use the operating income of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company to repay the loan of Decoration Company. On December 13, 2000, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and BOC Shudu Sub-branch signed an "Agreement on Extension of Loan Repayment", extending the repayment of the RMB 5 million loan due on December 16, 2000 under the "Loan Contract" to August 15, 2001, with the loan interest rate to be implemented at a monthly rate of 5.445 per thousand from the date of extension. After the above loans became due, Decoration Company performed part of its repayment obligations. BOC Shudu Sub-branch successively sent a "Notice of Loan Collection" and a "Notice to Urge Prompt Performance of Guarantee Obligations" to Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company on January 28, 2003, and May 17, 2004. The "Notice to Urge Prompt Repayment of Loan Principal and Interest" and the "Notice to Urge Prompt Performance of Guarantee Obligations" delivered on May 17, 2004, stated that as of May 17, 2004, Decoration Company still owed loan principal of RMB 19.91 million and overdue interest of RMB 14,173,340.44. Decoration Company signed to confirm, and Entertainment Company and Real Estate Company affixed their seals to promise to continue to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the above loan.

On June 25, 2004, BOC Shudu Sub-branch and Cinda Chengdu Office signed an "Assignment Agreement of Creditor's Rights". BOC Shudu Sub-branch assigned all creditor's rights involved in the case to Cinda Chengdu Office, and the transfer list recorded that as of May 31, 2004, Decoration Company still owed loan principal of RMB 19.86 million. On August 19, 2004, BOC Shudu Sub-branch served a "Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights" to Decoration Company, and simultaneously served a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights" to Real Estate Company and Entertainment Company, informing Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company to perform their repayment obligations and guarantee obligations to Cinda Chengdu Office. On June 17, 2006, the "Announcement of Creditor's Rights Collection" published by Cinda Chengdu Office in the newspaper stated: "...The debtors and corresponding guarantors of the following creditor's rights...shall perform their repayment obligations to Cinda Chengdu Office", and the collection content for the involved creditor's rights was: borrower Decoration Company, guarantors Decoration Company and Real Estate Company, guarantee contract number: Zhong Cheng Shu Fen Di Zi No. 99-001.

Further facts found: Decoration Company was a wholly Hong Kong-owned enterprise established in 1993 by Shen Brothers Investment (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shen Company), with a registered capital of RMB 10.32 million. In 2004, its business registration was changed to a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, with shareholders being Entertainment Company and Shen Company. Real Estate Company was established in 1992 by Shen Company, categorized as a wholly Hong Kong-owned enterprise, with a registered capital of USD 3 million. Entertainment Company was established in 1995, with shareholders being Real Estate Company and Decoration Company, and a registered capital of RMB 500,000. The legal representatives of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company were all Shen Huayuan. The three companies had the same address and telephone numbers, and their financial management personnel overlapped during the same periods.

Decoration Company's 2000 annual audit report reflected that most of Decoration Company's loans were invested in other companies, and a small portion was not for the company's own operational needs but for fundraising for companies within the group.

The "Overview of Business Development and Loan Extension Report" issued by Decoration Company in the name of Tailai Group to BOC Shudu Sub-branch, and the 2000 annual balance sheets of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company stated: Decoration Company directly used its income for the construction, decoration, and finishing of the China Wine City project. As of November 2000, among the total assets of Tailai Group amounting to RMB 223 million, Entertainment Company's assets were RMB 143 million, Real Estate Company's assets were RMB 76 million, and Decoration Company's assets were RMB 2 million. Among the total loans of Tailai Group amounting to RMB 171 million, Entertainment Company's loan was RMB 500,000, Real Estate Company's loan was RMB 51.75 million, and Decoration Company's loan was RMB 104 million. Entertainment Company and Real Estate Company promised that their earnings would be given priority to pay the principal and interest under the "Loan Contract" in this case.

The notes to the accounting statements in Entertainment Company's 1998 annual audit report indicated that among the bank deposit accounts, there were two accounts that paid the loan interest of Decoration Company and Real Estate Company.

Entertainment Company's 1998 annual audit report stated: as of 1998, total assets reached RMB 109 million, net assets were RMB 83.15 million, and the amounts of RMB 73.92 million owed to Decoration Company and RMB 10.86 million owed to Real Estate Company were converted into capital reserve funds totaling RMB 84.78 million through the method of converting liabilities into investments. Decoration Company's 2001-2005 annual audit reports and notes to the accounting statements showed that Decoration Company had long-term investments, and from 2003 to 2005, Decoration Company's investment in Entertainment Company amounted to RMB 27.95 million.

The "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the (2000) Cheng Zheng Nei Jing Zi No. 19314 "Notarial Deed" stated: Decoration Company and Real Estate Company promised to BOC Shudu Sub-branch that they had ownership and disposal rights over the assets of the "Golden Years" and "Yinmeng Lake" projects located within the China Wine City and registered under Entertainment Company's name.

The 1999 capital verification report of Real Estate Company showed: On June 3, 1999, Real Estate Company's shareholder, Shen Company, paid a design fee of USD 870,000 for the China Wine City project on behalf of Real Estate Company to Shi'an (International) Design Co., Ltd. in Hong Kong, and used this amount as Real Estate Company's contributed capital.

Documents from Decoration Company to BOC Shudu Sub-branch in the name of Tailai Group indicated: the operating income from the China Wine City project was used to pay for Tailai Group's rent, utilities, employee salaries, etc.; and it was acknowledged that the decreased capacity to pay loan interest was due to the development of the China Wine City project.

It was also found that Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company claimed that "Yinmeng Lake" and "Golden Years" were not registered trademarks, and Cinda Chengdu Office raised no objection to this.

Cinda Chengdu Office alleged in the first-instance complaint: The loan relationship between BOC Shudu Sub-branch and Decoration Company was genuine and legal, and Decoration Company should perform its repayment obligations. The aforementioned mortgage contracts were valid and legal, and Cinda Chengdu Office should legally enjoy the mortgage rights over the mortgaged property. The expressions of intent by Real Estate Company and Entertainment Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the loan were genuine and legal, and they should bear joint and several liability for discharge for the above loan. Moreover, the assets of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company were commingled, and their entities were confused, in substance constituting the same entity. Therefore, Real Estate Company and Entertainment Company should also bear joint and several liability for Decoration Company's debts according to law. Accordingly, Cinda Chengdu Office requested the court to: 1. Order Decoration Company to repay Cinda Chengdu Office the loan principal of RMB 19.86 million and pay the corresponding interest (interest as of December 20, 2006 was RMB 22,086,348.59); 2. Order Real Estate Company and Entertainment Company to bear joint and several liability for discharge for the above debts; 3. Confirm that Cinda Chengdu Office had mortgage rights over the following property and rights of the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites and the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant invested and operated by Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company within the China Wine City: a. All property; b. Project operating rights; c. Usage rights of buildings and ancillary buildings, and be entitled to priority compensation from the proceeds of auction or sale of the above property and rights or the fruits generated therefrom (the scope of priority compensation includes but is not limited to the loan principal, interest, and expenses for realizing the creditor's rights and mortgage rights); 4. Order Decoration Company to bear all litigation costs and preservation costs of this case, and Real Estate Company and Entertainment Company to bear joint and several liability for discharge for such costs.

The Sichuan High People's Court held through trial: The "Loan Contract" and the "Agreement on Extension of Loan Repayment" signed by the parties in this case represented the true intent of both contracting parties, and the parties had the requisite qualifications. The content of the contracts did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations, and therefore they should all be deemed valid.

After the "Loan Contract" was signed, BOC Shudu Sub-branch performed the loan disbursement obligation as agreed. After the loan became due, Decoration Company only repaid part of the loan principal and failed to perform the obligation to repay the full loan principal and interest as stipulated in the "Loan Contract", constituting a breach of contract. Therefore, Decoration Company should bear the liability for breach of contract for overdue repayment. Since the involved loan had been assigned by BOC Shudu Sub-branch to Cinda Chengdu Office through an "Assignment Agreement of Creditor's Rights" dated June 25, 2004, and Decoration Company had been notified, Cinda Chengdu Office legally acquired the creditor's rights against Decoration Company. Cinda Chengdu Office's claim to order Decoration Company to repay the remaining loan principal of RMB 19.86 million and the corresponding interest was established, and the court supported it accordingly.

The first-instance court held that the focus of the dispute in this case was: 1. Whether Entertainment Company and Real Estate Company should bear mortgage guarantee liability. Whether the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract" signed by Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and BOC Shudu Sub-branch represented the true intent of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company. Cinda Chengdu Office argued that the aforementioned mortgage contracts were valid and legal, and after Cinda Chengdu Office acquired the involved creditor's rights, it should legally enjoy the mortgage rights. Decoration Company argued that the loan did not provide mortgage guarantee to the creditor; Entertainment Company argued that it had no intent to create a mortgage over its property, and the mortgage right was not established; Real Estate Company argued that it had no right to dispose of Entertainment Company's property, and the mortgage was invalid. The court held that the basis for BOC Shudu Sub-branch to sign the "Loan Contract" with Decoration Company was the "Debt Restructuring Agreement" signed by Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company with BOC Shudu Sub-branch, and the "Letters of Guarantee" issued by Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company to BOC Shudu Sub-branch. In the "Debt Restructuring Agreement" and the "Letters of Guarantee", Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company all indicated that they would use the operational usage rights, all assets, and other related rights and interests of the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites under the "Southwest Celebrity Club" project as collateral for Decoration Company's loan. Therefore, before the "Loan Contract" was signed, Entertainment Company had already expressed its intention to create a mortgage over its property. Although Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company were independent legal persons, their legal representatives were all Shen Huayuan, and Decoration Company and Real Estate Company, who signed the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract", were the sole shareholders of Entertainment Company. Therefore, Entertainment Company must have been aware that Decoration Company and Real Estate Company were mortgaging its property. Despite being aware, Entertainment Company made no expression of denial regarding Decoration Company's and Real Estate Company's disposal actions, which should be deemed as consent to the disposal of its property. Finding that the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract" represented the common intent of Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company was consistent with the spirit of the principle of good faith. Taking into account the above factors, the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and the "Supplementary Contract" in this case were the true intent of BOC Shudu Sub-branch, Decoration Company, Real Estate Company, and Entertainment Company, and should be valid.

The Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and the Supplementary Contract: Whether the Properties and Rights Thereunder Can Serve as Subject Matter of a Mortgage. The Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and the Supplementary Contract explicitly stipulate that the project operating rights to be mortgaged are the trademark use rights for "Yinmeng Lake" and "Liujinsuiyue", the use rights for the buildings and ancillary buildings where the project is located, and the ownership of all property under the project; the ownership of property under the project is the value of the renovation, expansion, and decoration works and equipment of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites as set forth in the Asset Appraisal Report. Therefore, the properties and rights for which the Chengdu Office of Cinda requests enforcement of the mortgage are the trademark use rights for "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake", the use rights for the buildings and ancillary buildings where the project is located, and the equipment, renovation, expansion, and decoration works of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites.
1. Whether the trademark use rights for "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake" can be mortgaged. The court is of the opinion that, pursuant to Article 3 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, a trademark registrant enjoys the exclusive right to use a trademark, which is protected by law. Pursuant to Article 75(3) of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Security Law), the exclusive right to use a trademark may be pledged. Therefore, the law protects the exclusive right to use a trademark enjoyed by the holder of a registered trademark, and such exclusive right is a right that may be pledged, not a property that may be mortgaged. In this case, "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake" are not registered trademarks, and the rights enjoyed over them are not protected by law. The mortgage established by the parties over the use rights of the unregistered trademarks "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake" is invalid.
2. Whether the use rights for buildings and ancillary buildings can be used to establish a mortgage. The court is of the opinion that the use rights of the Entertainment Company over the buildings and ancillary buildings of the Chinese Wine City are derived from a lease relationship. The Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company are not the owners of the buildings and do not enjoy the right to dispose of the buildings and ancillary buildings; therefore, such use rights cannot serve as the subject matter of a mortgage contract. A mortgage established over the use rights of leased buildings and ancillary buildings is invalid, and no mortgage right has been created.
3. The validity of the mortgage over the equipment of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites. Pursuant to Article 42 of the Security Law, the mortgage of enterprise equipment and other movable property shall be registered with the administrative department for industry and commerce at the place where the property is located. In this case, after the parties signed the aforementioned mortgage contracts, the Supplementary Contract was registered with the Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce. The court is of the opinion that the equipment list attached to the Asset Appraisal Report is an appendix to the Supplementary Contract, and the registration of the Supplementary Contract constitutes registration of the equipment listed in the appendix. Therefore, the mortgage of the equipment in this case has undergone the statutory registration procedures, is valid, and the Chengdu Office of Cinda enjoys the mortgage right in accordance with the law. The arguments of the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company that the registration of the Supplementary Contract does not constitute registration of the mortgaged property and that the mortgage right has not been created are untenable, and the court does not support them.
4. Whether the renovation, expansion, and decoration works can be mortgaged. The court is of the opinion that the renovation, expansion, and decoration of the leased buildings by the Entertainment Company constitute an act of attachment by the user to the buildings. Pursuant to Article 86 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation), if a non-owner adds attachments to the property of another person, and the owner of the property consents to the addition and reaches an agreement on how to handle the attachments upon return of the property, the matter shall be handled according to the agreement; if there is no agreement and negotiation fails, if the attachments can be dismantled, the court may order their removal; if they cannot be dismantled, the attachments may be appraised and transferred to the property owner; if loss is caused to the property owner, the person adding the attachments shall bear liability for compensation. It can be seen that where attachments are added to another's property, the non-owner and the property owner shall follow their agreement; if there is no agreement and the attachments cannot be dismantled, the original property owner acquires ownership. In this case, if dismantled, the renovation, expansion, and decoration works of the leased buildings by the Entertainment Company would lose their economic value; they cannot exist independently apart from the original buildings, nor can they be separately appraised or sold to realize the mortgage right. Without the consent of the building owner, the Entertainment Company has no right to dispose of them. Furthermore, the lease contract does not stipulate that the building owner shall compensate for the decoration part when reclaiming the leased buildings. Therefore, the renovation, expansion, and decoration works cannot constitute mortgaged property. The mortgage of the renovation, expansion, and decoration works is invalid, and no mortgage right has been created.
II. Whether the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company shall bear joint and several guaranty liability. The Chengdu Office of Cinda argues that the commitments made by the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company in the Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Principal and Interest Repayment Plan constitute expressions of intent to assume joint and several guaranty liability for the debts of the Decoration Company, and that the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company repeatedly confirmed this in the Loan Repayment Reminder Notice, making the guarantee valid. The court is of the opinion that the Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch did not enter into a written guarantee contract with the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company. In the Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Principal and Interest Repayment Plan issued by the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company to the Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch, the commitment by the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company to repay the Decoration Company's debts using the companies' operating revenues constitutes an expression of intent for debt assumption, without any clear indication of agreeing to assume guaranty liability, and thus cannot serve as the basis for establishing guaranty liability. In the Notice Urging the Performance of Guaranty Obligations issued by the Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch on May 17, 2004, the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company for the first time explicitly committed to assume joint and several guaranty liability for the loans of the Decoration Company. Therefore, it shall be determined that the guarantee relationship was established from that date. The Entertainment Company and the Housing Company argue that the guarantee claim held by the Chengdu Office of Cinda has exceeded the statute of limitations. The court is of the opinion that after the Chengdu Office of Cinda acquired the claims in question, the Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch issued a Notice of Transfer of Guaranty Rights to the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company on August 19, 2004, and the signing and receipt thereof by the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company caused an interruption of the statute of limitations for the guarantee claim. Therefore, the statute of limitations for the Chengdu Office of Cinda to demand that the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company assume guaranty liability should have continued until August 19, 2006. As for whether the debt collection announcement published by the Chengdu Office of Cinda in the newspaper on June 17, 2006, could cause an interruption of the statute of limitations, the court is of the opinion that since the parties did not enter into a formal guarantee contract, the guarantee relationship could not be stated in the column for guarantee contracts in the collection announcement. Listing the guarantor constitutes a demand for the guarantee claim. In the collection announcement, the Chengdu Office of Cinda listed the Housing Company in the guarantor column, which should be regarded as a demand for the guarantee claim against the Housing Company. Therefore, the statute of limitations for the guarantee claim held by the Chengdu Office of Cinda against the Housing Company was interrupted again on June 17, 2006. As of January 22, 2007, when the Chengdu Office of Cinda filed the lawsuit with this court demanding that the Housing Company assume guaranty liability, the statute of limitations had not yet expired, and this court protects its claim in accordance with the law. As for the guarantee claim held by the Chengdu Office of Cinda against the Entertainment Company, since no demand was made in the collection announcement, and the Chengdu Office of Cinda also failed to provide evidence that it had asserted its rights against the Entertainment Company by other means before the expiration of the statute of limitations on August 19, 2006, therefore, as of January 22, 2007, when the Chengdu Office of Cinda filed the lawsuit demanding that the Entertainment Company assume guaranty liability, the statute of limitations had expired, and the Chengdu Office of Cinda has lost its right to win the lawsuit. The Entertainment Company's defense is well-founded.
III. The issue of whether there exists confusion of personality among the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company, and the issue of liability. The Chengdu Office of Cinda argues that although the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company are limited liability companies, they are controlled by the same actual controller, have no independent property or personality, the Decoration Company and the Housing Company have transferred a large amount of property to the Entertainment Company, resulting in confusion of property and confusion of subjects with the Entertainment Company, and therefore the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of the Decoration Company. The court is of the opinion that the equity relationships of the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company are intertwined; in fact, all three were established with capital contributions from the Shenshi Company. Shen Huayuan, as the chairman of the board of all three companies, holds absolute control over the companies. In this situation, Shen Huayuan should have strictly adhered to the principle of separation of property, fully maintained the corporate system and the company's interests, in accordance with the principles of good faith and prohibition of abuse of rights. However, in this case, Shen Huayuan ignored the independent personalities of the three companies, abused his control over the companies, and injected a large amount of the Decoration Company's loans into the Entertainment Company's Chinese Wine City project; without undergoing the procedures for change of industrial and commercial registration, he converted the Entertainment Company's debts owed to the Decoration Company of RMB 73.92 million and the housing company's debts of RMB 10.86 million into capital contributions from the two companies to the Entertainment Company, and after 2003, the Decoration Company's investment in the Entertainment Company amounted to only RMB 27.95 million, while RMB 35.97 million of the Decoration Company's investment funds were unaccounted for; the operating income from the Chinese Wine City project was used to pay the rent, utilities, and employee salaries of all companies under the Tailai Group; the Shenshi Company's investment in the Housing Company was used to pay the design fees for the Chinese Wine City project; the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company also jointly repaid the principal and interest on the Decoration Company's loans. All these facts indicate that the personalities and property of the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company have been continuously confused. The Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company all believe that they have the right to dispose of the assets of the "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake" projects, and they issued letters to the lender in the name of the non-existent Tailai Group, making it impossible for the lender to distinguish between the personalities and property of the three entities. The fact that the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company operated at the same address, shared the same telephone number, and had the same financial management personnel for a period of time is also a manifestation of Shen Huayuan's abuse of control and confusion of corporate personalities. The Decoration Company is unable to repay a large amount of overdue debts, which damages the legitimate rights and interests of the lender. Shen Huayuan, through his control over the companies, used the independent corporate personality to evade debts, which violates the purpose of the legal person system and the principles of good faith and fairness. Therefore, the debts of the Decoration Company shall be borne by the Entertainment Company and the Housing Company under joint and several liability. The court supports this claim of the Chengdu Office of Cinda.

In summary, the Decoration Company has overdue debts owed to the Chengdu Office of Cinda and refuses to repay. The Chengdu Office of Cinda's claim for repayment of principal and interest by the Decoration Company shall be supported. The Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and the Supplementary Contract signed with the Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch represent the true intention of the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company, and the mortgaged property, i.e., the equipment of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites, has undergone the statutory mortgage registration procedures. Therefore, within the limit of the maximum amount of RMB 22 million, the Chengdu Office of Cinda has the right to enforce the mortgage right over the above property for debts under the Loan Contract that cannot be repaid. As for other mortgaged properties under the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and the Supplementary Contract, namely the trademark use rights for "Liujinsuiyue" and "Yinmeng Lake", the use rights for the buildings and ancillary buildings where the project is located, and the renovation, expansion, and decoration works, since they cannot serve as the subject matter of a mortgage, the mortgage is invalid. Therefore, the claim of the Chengdu Office of Cinda to enforce the mortgage right over the above property is untenable, and the court does not support it. Although the Entertainment Company is a joint and several guarantor for the debts involved in this case, the Chengdu Office of Cinda did not make a demand within the statute of limitations for the guarantee claim. Therefore, the court does not support the claim of the Chengdu Office of Cinda to require the Entertainment Company to assume guarantor liability. The Housing Company provided joint and several guaranty for the debts involved in this case, and the Chengdu Office of Cinda also made a demand within the statute of limitations for the guarantee claim. Therefore, the Housing Company shall bear joint and several liability for repaying the debts that the Decoration Company cannot repay. The personalities and property of the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company are confused. The Entertainment Company and the Housing Company shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of the Decoration Company. Pursuant to Article 128, paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of Article 134 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 4, 135, 137, and 140 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, paragraphs 1 of Article 60, paragraph 1 of Article 80, Article 81, Articles 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 18, 34, 41, item (5) of Article 42, and Article 53 of the Security Law, the judgment is as follows:
1. The Decoration Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, repay the Chengdu Office of Cinda the loan principal of RMB 19.86 million and the interest (calculation of interest: as of May 17, 2004, the interest was RMB 14,173,340.44; from May 17, 2006 to June 25, 2006, the date of assignment of the claim, interest shall be calculated in accordance with the Loan Contract; from the date of assignment of the claim to the date of full payment, interest shall be calculated in accordance with the relevant overdue interest rate provisions of the People's Bank of China);
2. Within the limit of the maximum amount of RMB 22 million for the above debts of the Decoration Company, the Chengdu Office of Cinda has a mortgage right over the equipment of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites as listed in the Asset Appraisal Reports (Ping (98) No. 14 and Ping (98) No. 15) issued by Jianhua Certified Public Accountants, and has the right to be repaid in priority from the proceeds of the auction or sale thereof;
3. The Housing Company and the Entertainment Company shall bear joint and several liability for repaying the above debts of the Decoration Company;
4. The other claims of the Chengdu Office of Cinda are dismissed. If the Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company fail to fulfill the monetary obligations within the period specified in this judgment, they shall, in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, double the interest on debts for the period of delayed performance. The case acceptance fee is RMB 109,870, other litigation fees are RMB 21,974, and the property preservation fee is RMB 110,260, totaling RMB 242,104. The Decoration Company shall bear RMB 80,701.34, the Housing Company shall bear RMB 80,701.33, and the Entertainment Company shall bear RMB 80,701.33.

The Decoration Company, the Housing Company, and the Entertainment Company all disagreed with the above civil judgment of the original trial court and filed appeals to this court respectively. Their common grounds of appeal and reasons are as follows: The first instance court erroneously determined that the subjects of the three appellants were confused based on the fact that "the three defendants operated at the same address, shared the same telephone number, and had the same financial management personnel for a period of time." In 1992, the Shenshi Company obtained approval to register the Housing Company with a registered capital of USD 3 million, engaged in the development, construction, and operation of production-use buildings, with Shen Huayuan as the legal representative. In 1993, the Shenshi Company obtained approval to register the Decoration Company with a registered capital of USD 500,000, engaged in decoration design for various types of buildings, with Shen Huayuan as the legal representative. In 2005, the Entertainment Company injected RMB 6 million in capital, and the registered capital increased to RMB 10.32 million. In 1995, the Housing Company and the Decoration Company, both foreign-invested enterprises, jointly established the Entertainment Company, engaged in cultural, entertainment, sports, and catering projects, with Shen Huayuan as the legal representative. The Housing Company, the Decoration Company, and the Entertainment Company were all registered as enterprise legal persons with the industry and commerce bureau in accordance with the law. The three companies were invested in by the Shenshi Company, each having its own business scope and financial accounting, and always conducted lawful business within their respective business scopes as independent legal persons. The financial systems of the three companies were sound and independent, and the claims and debts between the companies were clear. This is also supported by the annual independent audits, which indicate that each company has clear and independent financial accounting and property ownership boundaries. Therefore, the three appellants do not have confusion of personality. If indeed the first instance wrongly determined that the three appellants had subject confusion, the original creditor, the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda, and the first instance judgment would have recognized that fact, and there would have been no need for the original creditor to go to great lengths to sign the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, and the extensions and supplements thereof, such as the Guarantee letter, the Supplementary Contract, and the Principal and Interest Repayment Plan. In summary, the facts found by the first instance are true, but in determining the case according to law, it failed to pay attention to the essential nature, internal connections, and potential illegal causal relationships of the existing facts. After finding flaws in various evidence and determining that parts of the agreement are invalid, it erroneously concluded that the subjects were confused.

Additionally, the Decoration Company and the Housing Company appeal to this court, arguing that the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, the Guarantee letter, the Supplementary Contract to the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, and the Principal and Interest Repayment Plan involved in this case were invalid contracts signed by the appellants under the inducement of the original creditor, the Bank of China Chengdu Branch, in violation of the principle of fairness, for the purpose of transferring non-performing loans. According to the Debt Restructuring Agreement signed between the Decoration Company and the original creditor, it has been proven that the Decoration Company was unable to repay the loan as agreed, which was an objective fact known to the creditor at that time. Instead of writing off the non-performing loan as it should have, the original creditor repeatedly induced the appellants to sign the above contracts, citing that "all business of the Bank of China Chengdu Branch is now transferred to the Chengdu Shudu Avenue Sub-branch." This constitutes fraudulent conduct by the original creditor against the appellant Decoration Company and Housing Company, which was obviously unfair, and the above contracts are invalid.

The Housing Company further appeals to this court, arguing: 1. As stated above, since the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Supplementary Contract, and other agreements are invalid, the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda does not enjoy the mortgage right over the equipment of the "Liujinsuiyue" Western Restaurant and the "Yinmeng Lake" Urban Hot Spring Business Suites. Moreover, pursuant to Articles 41 and 42 of the Security Law, a mortgage over enterprise equipment and other movable property shall be registered as mortgaged property. Since the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda did not separately register the mortgage for each piece of the enterprise's movable property, but only registered the entire Supplementary Contract, the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda does not enjoy the mortgage right over the movable property, i.e., the equipment. 2. The Guarantee letter, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Supplementary Contract, and other agreements involved in this case were signed under conditions of obvious unfairness and fraud, and are invalid. Therefore, the appellant Housing Company is not obligated to assume guaranty liability. At the same time, the original trial court, based solely on the reason that the guarantee relationship could not be stated in the collection announcement, held that listing the guarantor constituted a demand for the guarantee claim. This view is erroneous. It must be emphasized: The appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda published a collection announcement in the newspaper based on the "Guarantee Contract Number" — Zhongcheng Shufen Di Zi 99 No. 001, which is a mortgage contract, not a guarantee contract. Moreover, the heading of the newspaper where the collection announcement was published read, "Pursuant to the following loan contracts and guarantee contracts, please contact the borrowers and corresponding guarantors of the following claims..." From this, it can be seen that the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda made this representation based on a specific document. The court should not render any arbitrary or expansive interpretation. Therefore, the publication of the collection announcement by the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda cannot cause an interruption of the statute of limitations for the guaranty liability. Because the statute of limitations for the guaranty liability has expired, the appellant Housing Company is not obligated to assume guaranty liability.

In summary, the three appellants all request: The court shall, in accordance with the law, set aside items 1, 2, and 3 of the original judgment and sustain item 4; the litigation costs of the first instance and the appeal shall be borne by the appellee Chengdu Office of Cinda.

The Appellee, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office, responded to the joint appeal claims and arguments of Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company as follows: The corporate personalities of the three appellants have been continuously confused. Specifically with regard to the debt involved in this case, the three appellants clearly constituted a confusion of borrower identities and a relationship of joint debtors. The aforesaid continuous and specific confusion of the three appellants has seriously harmed the lawful rights and interests of the creditor. The first-instance judgment, which ordered the three appellants to bear joint and several liability for repayment of the debt involved in this case, has clear facts, sufficient evidence, and correct application of law.

Furthermore, the Appellee, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office, responded to the appeal claims and arguments of Decoration Company and Housing Company as follows: The legal documents such as the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, and the Letter of Guarantee were sealed and signed by all parties. They represent the true intentions of the parties and do not involve any circumstance under Article 52 of the Contract Law that would render the contract void. They have been lawfully formed and have taken effect, and are legally binding on all parties. In the first instance, the three appellants admitted the validity of the aforesaid contracts and undertakings and the fact that they had been partially performed. The so-called fraudulent inducement by Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch, as alleged by the appellants, simply does not exist. The first-instance judgment clearly found the facts, had sufficient evidence, and correctly applied the law.

The Appellee, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office, responded to the appeal claims and arguments of Housing Company regarding the mortgage rights and guarantee liability as follows: First, the Creditor's Demand for Payment Notice issued by Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office caused the suspension of the statute of limitations for Housing Company's guarantee debt. Housing Company should continue to bear joint and several liability for repayment of Decoration Company's debt to the Appellee, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office. Second, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and its Supplemental Contract, under which Decoration Company and Housing Company mortgaged all equipment of the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant and the "Dreamlike Lake" City Hot Spring Business Suite to the Appellee, represented the true intentions of the three appellants. They have been lawfully formed and have taken effect, and are legally binding on the three appellants. The mortgage underwent the registration procedures required by the Security Law, and the Appellee holds a mortgage right over the aforesaid equipment.

In summary, the appeal requests of the appellants Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company all lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed in their entirety. The first-instance judgment clearly found the facts, had sufficient and reliable evidence, and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed in its entirety.

During the second instance of this case, the appellant Housing Company submitted to this Court a "Request for Judicial Expertise," requesting a forensic examination of the authenticity of two documents dated May 17, 2004, and August 19, 2004, which were stamped with the official seal of Housing Company and were titled "Notice Urging Prompt Repayment of Loan Principal and Interest" and "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights." Upon examination, in the first instance, the three appellants, including Housing Company, raised no objection to the authenticity of these two documents. In the second instance, the appellant Housing Company also failed to produce sufficient evidence to negate the authenticity of the aforesaid two documents. Therefore, this Court does not accept Housing Company's request for forensic examination.

The facts found by the court of first instance are hereby affirmed by this Court.

Upon trial, this Court is of the opinion that: Based on the appeal claims and defense opinions of the parties to this case, the disputed issues among the parties are whether the relevant agreements involved in this case, such as the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, and the Letter of Guarantee, are legally valid; whether Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company have confused corporate personalities; whether Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office holds a mortgage right over the movable property, i.e., the equipment; and whether Housing Company should bear guarantee liability.

1. Regarding the issue of whether the relevant agreements such as the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, and the Letter of Guarantee are legally valid. First, the execution of the aforesaid agreements represented the true intention of both parties. Their content does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and there is no circumstance under Article 52 of the Contract Law that would render the contract void. The aforesaid contracts and agreements are legally valid and are legally binding on both parties. Second, in the first instance, the three appellants admitted the validity of the relevant agreements such as the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Loan Contract, and the Letter of Guarantee, and the fact that they had been partially performed. In the second instance, Decoration Company and Housing Company also failed to produce evidence proving the existence of any grounds for invalidity of the aforesaid agreements. Therefore, the appeal arguments of the appellants Decoration Company and Housing Company, that Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch engaged in fraudulent inducement and that the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, the Supplemental Contract, and the Letter of Guarantee involved in this case were executed under circumstances of obvious unfairness or fraud and are thus void, lack factual and legal basis, and are not supported by this Court.

2. Regarding the issue of whether Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company have confused corporate personalities. According to the facts found by the court of first instance in this case, Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company have cross-shareholding relationships and are all affiliated companies. They were all actually invested in by Shen's Company. Shen Huayuan, as the chairman of the board of directors of the companies, concurrently served as the legal representative of all three companies. Using his control over the three companies, he invested a large amount of the loan obtained by Decoration Company into the China Wine City project of Entertainment Company. Without completing the industrial and commercial registration for change, he converted Entertainment Company's debts of RMB 73.92 million to Decoration Company and RMB 10.86 million to Housing Company into investment by the two companies in Entertainment Company. After 2003, Decoration Company's investment in Entertainment Company amounted to only RMB 27.95 million, while the whereabouts of RMB 35.97 million of Decoration Company's investment funds were unknown. The operating income from the China Wine City project was used to pay rent, utilities, and employee salaries for all companies under the so-called Tailai Group. Shen's Company's investment in Housing Company was used to pay design fees for the China Wine City project. Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company also jointly repaid the principal and interest on loans obtained by Decoration Company. All three companies considered themselves entitled to dispose of the assets of the "Golden Years" and "Dreamlike Lake" projects. They issued letters to the lender in the name of the non-existent Tailai Group, making it impossible for the lender to distinguish between the personnel and assets of the three entities. Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company also shared the same office address, telephone number, and had the same financial management personnel for a period. The above facts show that although Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company were ostensibly independent companies, they had in fact formed a confusion of corporate personalities among themselves. Their conduct contravened the purpose of establishing the corporate entity system, violated the principles of good faith and fairness, and harmed the interests of creditors. Therefore, the court of first instance correctly ordered that Entertainment Company and Housing Company should bear joint and several liability for repayment of Decoration Company's debts, and this Court affirms that decision.

3. Regarding the issue of whether Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office holds a mortgage right over the movable property, i.e., the equipment. In the Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Letter of Guarantee involved in this case, Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company all indicated that the operating rights, all assets, and other related rights and interests of the "Golden Years" Western Restaurant and the "Dreamlike Lake" City Hot Spring Business Suite in the "Southwest Famous Club" project would be used as collateral for the loan of Decoration Company. Therefore, before the Loan Contract was executed between Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch and Decoration Company, Entertainment Company had already expressed its intention to create a mortgage using its own property. The legal representatives of Decoration Company, Housing Company, and Entertainment Company were all Shen Huayuan. Moreover, Decoration Company and Housing Company, which executed the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract and the Supplemental Contract, were the sole shareholders of Entertainment Company. Therefore, Entertainment Company must have been aware of the mortgage of its property by Decoration Company and Housing Company. Since Entertainment Company did not express any intention to deny this, it should be deemed to have consented to the disposition of its property. After executing the aforementioned mortgage contracts, the parties registered the Supplemental Contract with the Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce. The equipment list attached to the Asset Appraisal Report was an appendix to the Supplemental Contract. Registration of the Supplemental Contract constitutes registration of the equipment listed in the appendix. Therefore, the mortgage over the relevant equipment in this case underwent the statutory registration procedures, complying with Article 42 of the Security Law, which provides that "...for mortgages on equipment and other movable property of an enterprise, the registration authority is the administration for industry and commerce at the place where the property is located." Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office legally holds a mortgage right over the mortgaged property. Therefore, the appeal argument of the appellant Housing Company, that registration of the Supplemental Contract does not constitute registration of the mortgaged property and that the Appellee, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office, does not hold a mortgage right over the movable property, i.e., the equipment, lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this Court.

4. Regarding the issue of whether Housing Company should bear guarantee liability. In the "Notice Urging Prompt Fulfillment of Guarantee Liability" issued by Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch on May 17, 2004, Housing Company expressly undertook to bear joint and several guarantee liability for the loan of Decoration Company, and the guarantee relationship was established from that date. After Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office acquired the debt involved in this case, Bank of China Shudu Sub-branch issued a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights" to Housing Company on August 19, 2004. Housing Company's acknowledgment of receipt of this notice caused the suspension of the statute of limitations for the guaranteed claim. On June 17, 2006, Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office published a collection notice in the newspaper and listed Housing Company in the security contract column of the collection notice. This should be regarded as an assertion of the guaranteed claim against Housing Company, meaning the statute of limitations for the guaranteed claim was again suspended on June 17, 2006. Therefore, when Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on January 22, 2007, seeking Housing Company's assumption of guarantee liability, the statute of limitations had not expired. Consequently, this Court does not support Housing Company's argument that, after making a specific undertaking, it should be relieved of liability on the ground that the creditor Cinda Asset Management Chengdu Office's exercise of the guarantee claim was beyond the time limit and therefore its promise should be denied.

In summary, the first-instance judgment clearly found the facts and correctly applied the law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby orders as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance and the property preservation fee shall be executed according to the first-instance judgment. The court acceptance fee for the second instance, amounting to RMB 659,220, shall be borne jointly by the appellants Sichuan Tailai Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd., Sichuan Tailai Housing Development Co., Ltd., and Sichuan Tailai Entertainment Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Judge: Zhu Hainian
